tagline: Access control written in English, decided by consensus.
summary: An owner writes an access policy in plain English. Anyone may ask whether a given wallet satisfies it. Five GenLayer validators independently PARSE the policy into structured conditions, independently FETCH the wallet's history from Blockscout on one of four chains, independently EVALUATE each condition in Python against the numbers they fetched, and agree on a seven-field feature vector. Any contract can then call is_granted(wallet, policy_id) and get a bool. The model reads the policy and is never shown a wallet; every decision is integer comparison on numbers five validators fetched separately.

consensus.axis: A seven-field feature vector joined into one string: verdict | conditions_met | conditions_total | wallet_age_bucket | tx_count_bucket | balance_bucket | content_hash. RETRY sits on the same axis because it is not a verdict - validators must AGREE that the explorer was transiently unavailable.
consensus.why_quantised: docs/PROBE.md §5: the same wallet fetched twice seconds apart returned DIFFERENT bodies on 5 of 7 captures - confirmations moves on every row of every chain, and Base additionally finished decoding method names between the two fetches. A raw digest on the axis would have disagreed on 4 of 4 chains; the quantised vector disagreed on 0 of 4.
consensus.content_hash: On the axis, and allowed there because it hashes NO explorer bytes: its inputs are the policy id, the policy text hash, the wallet, the chain, the canonical parse and the six other axis fields. It binds them together and can never itself be what validators fall out over.
consensus.evidence_digest: Stored on every check as evidence and NEVER voted on.
consensus.leader_cannot_forge: Wallet age, transaction count and balance are all on the axis in bucketed form, so a leader cannot report a four-year-old wallet where five validators saw a four-day-old one. _coherent additionally refuses a GRANTED that did not meet every condition, a GRANTED over zero conditions, and a GRANTED beside an unverifiable requirement.
consensus.conservative: Every fact carries a `known` flag and every condition can answer UNKNOWN. An unknown, an unverifiable requirement, a failed parse or an empty parse all give INCONCLUSIVE - never GRANTED. A lower-bound transaction count may prove a PASS and may never prove a FAIL.
consensus.no_raise: The contract contains ZERO raise statements and no payable method, both asserted by parsing the AST of the source and of the built artifact. A rejection is a successful transaction returning {"ok": false, "reason": ...}; the RETRY path writes nothing, so it needs no rollback.

endpoints.first_transaction: /api?module=account&action=txlist&sort=asc&page=1&offset=1 — read ONLY when the v2 page came back full; see docs/PROBE.md §4

seeded_policies.name: Ethereum Veteran
seeded_policies.policy_text: To pass this gate the wallet must be at least one year old measured from its very first transaction, must have made at least 100 transactions, must hold at least 0.01 ETH, and no more than 25 percent of its recent transactions may have failed.

seeded_policies.name: Base Early Adopter
seeded_policies.policy_text: The wallet must have been active on Base for at least six months since its first transaction, must have made at least 10 transactions, and must currently hold at least 0.001 ETH. No more than half of its recent transactions may have failed.

seeded_policies.name: Arbitrum Active Trader
seeded_policies.policy_text: Access requires a wallet at least 90 days old that has made at least 50 transactions on Arbitrum, with no more than 20 percent of its recent transactions having failed. There is no minimum balance requirement for this gate.

seeded_policies.name: Polygon Holder
seeded_policies.policy_text: The wallet must be at least 30 days old, must have made at least 5 transactions on Polygon, and must hold at least 1 POL. Up to 40 percent of its recent transactions may have failed; Polygon is cheap enough that people retry.

seeded_policies.name: Strict Council Seat
seeded_policies.policy_text: A council seat requires a wallet at least two years old with at least 500 transactions, holding at least 0.05 ETH. The holder must also have passed the foundation's off-chain identity verification and must be a resident of a jurisdiction where governance participation is permitted.

studiodev.artifact_note: The deployed bytes ARE the reviewed source, and that is checkable rather than asserted: `python3 tools/verify_onchain.py 0xB0F8bE23f9Ae0f53D818D0b9C68F6641c22500A4 build/PolicyGate.min.py` reads the code back off the chain with `genlayer code` and answers MATCH on sha256 e56dfc93b681611e... - not EQUIVALENT-under-renaming, the same bytes. `git checkout 93ada5c9 && bash tools/build.sh` reproduces them; contracts/PolicyGate.py and build/PolicyGate.min.py last changed in ae90abea, so every commit from there to HEAD builds this artifact. The source has not moved since this deploy, which is why the two commit fields above are equal.

verified.method: genlayer code <address> -> strip CLI chrome -> sha256, via tools/verify_onchain.py
verified.live_behaviour: get_policy on all five policies answered parse_stable: null with parse_runs: 0 at 2026-09-21T10:06:52Z - after the policies were created and before any check had run. That is the tri-state the review asked for, observed on the deployment rather than in the diff.

supersedes.why: Rejected in review for a source mismatch: it answered parse_stable: false for a policy nobody had checked yet, where the GitHub source answers null. It was one commit behind on a view field - no verdict, vector, storage shape or ABI differed - and it was kept rather than realigned because it held 16 decided checks. The record is left here because those checks and that decision are part of this project's history, but the rule now is that what is submitted is what is on chain. See contracts/NOTES.md 13.
